body:
_Migrated from issue #1233, filed 2026-07-29._

Affects both the classic editor and the new UI, and predates the new UI's custom-column editing (#1232) — that PR only made it easier to reach.

**Symptom.** Type exactly `None` into a custom column (a notes/comments column is the realistic case) and save. The value is not stored — the column is cleared instead.

**Cause.** `cps/editbooks.py::edit_cc_data_value` maps the literal string to Python `None` before it considers the column's datatype:

```python
if to_save[cc_string] == 'None':
    to_save[cc_string] = None
```

That is deliberate for `bool`: the classic editor's yes/no `<select>` in `cps/templates/book_edit.html` uses `<option value="None">` as its "unset" sentinel. For every other datatype the sentinel is meaningless — an int column cannot hold "None" anyway — but the check runs before the datatype branch, so a text or comments column loses a legitimate value.

**Likely fix.** Narrow the check to `c.datatype == 'bool'`. Worth confirming first that no other caller relies on the broad form: the classic editor's date fields clear via `''`, and `/api/v1`'s custom-column path (added in #1232) sends `''` for null and never emits the sentinel.

Needs a red/green test on the shared core, since both editors and the inline books-table editor route through it.

Found during the cross-family review of #1232 and deliberately not fixed there — changing a sentinel the classic bool select depends on should not ride along in a feature PR.
title: Typing the literal word "None" into a custom column clears it instead of saving it
